newsitem.title: UK: Kingfisher Q3 like-for-like sales up 7.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Kingfisher Q3 like-for-like sales up 7.5 pct.

text.p: Retail group Kingfisher Plc said on Wednesday that its like-for-like sales for the third quarter to November 2, 1996 grew 7.5 percent.
Total sales rose by 12.9 percent to 1.345 billion stg with its three main retail chains B&Q, Comet and Woolworths achieving double digit growth.
In a statement, Kingfisher said B&Q, its DIY chain, increased sales by 18.5 percent. "Its two formats -- supercentres and warehouses -- both achieved similar like-for-like increases," it said.
Woolworths sales for the same period rose 13.2 percent, mainly on gains made in the first half.
"This year's targeted roll-out of new format local stores was completed and there was now 117. The new format is increasing sales on average by 22 percent.
Comet, the company's electrical goods retailer, achieved a sales growth of 16.5 percent.
Darty, the group's French electricals division, increased sales by 2.3 percent at actual rates.
"At constant exchange rates, the sales increase was 2.0 percent, after adjusting for sales made by the Belgian subsidiary New Vanden Borre."
However, Darty's like-for-like sales inched up only by 0.4 percent in difficult trading conditions.
Kingfisher's Superdrug division achieved a sales hike of 6.6 percent with like-for-like sales climbing 5.4 percent.
